document_summary: This document is the Horizon Airlines Operations Manual, covering organizational governance, operational control, passenger services, and related airline operational procedures. It establishes standardized procedures derived from FAA, ICAO, IATA, and NBAA guidance, and includes a detailed first section on governance and a beginning second section on passenger services.

sections.section_summary: A list of operational categories covered by the Horizon Airlines Operations Manual, outlining the major areas of airline operations addressed in subsequent sections.

subsections.summary: Enumerates the major domains of airline operations covered in the manual.
key_points: Organization & Governance
Passenger Services (Check-In, Boarding, Baggage Handling)
Ground Operations (Aircraft Turnaround, Dispatch & Flight Planning)
OCC Operations and Crew Management
Safety Management System and Maintenance Coordination
Security Operations, Weather Disruptions, Delay & Cancellation Management
Emergency Response, Dangerous Goods, Training & Compliance

sections.section_summary: Provides attributions and source materials for the development of the Horizon Airlines Operations Manual, noting it is an original knowledge base derived from recognized aviation authorities and industry organizations.

subsections.summary: Explains the origin of the manual as an original airline operations knowledge base intended to support operational personnel, RAG systems, decision support tools, training programs, and AI assistants. Notes that content is synthesized from industry standards rather than reproduced verbatim.
key_points: Manual is original and intended for operational, RAG, training, and AI-assistant use
Derived from generally accepted aviation industry practices
Procedures must be reviewed against applicable regulations before live implementation
Horizon Airlines retains responsibility for adapting procedures to its specific environment

subsections.summary: Lists the ten primary reference materials that served as foundational guidance for the manual's development.
key_points: FAA Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge – Airport Operations
FAA Advisory Circular AC 120-71B – Standard Operating Procedures and Operational Guidance
ICAO Safety Management Manual (SMM) and Annexes/Operational Guidance
IATA Airport Handling Practices, Ground Operations Standards, and Dangerous Goods Regulations
NBAA Airplane Standard Operating Procedures Manual
UK Overseas Territories Aviation Circular (OTAC) Operations Manual Guidance
Publicly available airline operations manuals and aircraft manufacturer documentation

sections.section_summary: Establishes standardized operational procedures for Horizon Airlines, covering organizational structure, accountabilities, the Operations Control Center, decision-making hierarchy, and document control. This is the foundational governance section of the operations manual.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of the Operations Manual as establishing standardized procedures for safe, efficient, compliant, and customer-focused airline operations, serving as the primary operational reference for all departments.
key_points: Manual establishes standardized operational procedures for Horizon Airlines
Serves as the primary operational reference for all departments
Personnel must comply with procedures unless deviation is required to preserve life, safety, security, or regulatory compliance

subsections.summary: Outlines the core operational principles of Horizon Airlines, including safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.
key_points: Safety First: Safety takes precedence over efficiency, schedule, commercial, and financial objectives
No employee shall be penalized for delaying/cancelling operations due to legitimate safety concerns
Regulatory Compliance: Must comply with national aviation regulations, airport authority requirements, ATC instructions, company procedures, and manufacturer guidance
Continuous Improvement: Periodic reviews for safety, efficiency, training, and technology enhancements

subsections.summary: Describes the operational divisions of Horizon Airlines and their responsibilities.
key_points: Executive Management: Corporate strategy, regulatory oversight, financial management, safety policy approval
Operations Division: Daily flight operations, crew management, dispatch, operational control
Ground Operations Division: Aircraft turnaround, ramp operations, passenger handling, baggage handling
Technical Operations Division: Maintenance, airworthiness, engineering support, aircraft reliability
Safety Department: Risk management, safety investigations, compliance monitoring, safety reporting

subsections.summary: Defines the duties and responsibilities of key leadership roles in the airline.
key_points: CEO: Approves operational policies, allocates resources, ensures compliance, supports safety initiatives
Director of Operations: Oversees operational activities, ensures SOP compliance, manages disruptions, coordinates interdepartmental activities
Safety Manager: Maintains SMS, monitors safety performance, conducts risk assessments, coordinates investigations
OCC Manager: Supervises daily operations, monitors flight progress, manages disruptions, coordinates emergency responses

subsections.summary: Defines the OCC as the central coordination hub for airline operations that operates continuously and maintains situational awareness of key operational elements.
key_points: OCC serves as the central coordination hub
Operates continuously, monitoring aircraft locations, flight status, weather, airport conditions, crew availability, maintenance status, and security concerns

subsections.summary: Details the three core areas of OCC responsibility: flight monitoring, disruption management, and communication.
key_points: Flight Monitoring: Track all flights from departure to arrival, monitoring times, route deviations, fuel status, and aircraft performance
Disruption Management: Manage delays, diversions, cancellations, aircraft substitutions, and crew reassignments
Communication: Maintain contact with flight crews, airports, ground handling agents, maintenance control, and executive management

subsections.summary: Specifies the conditions that must be met before a flight may be dispatched, covering aircraft, crew, environmental, and airport requirements.
key_points: Aircraft must be airworthy, free of unresolved critical defects, and meet operational requirements
Crew must be qualified, medically fit, meet duty time requirements, and possess required certifications
Weather must meet operational minima and not create unacceptable risk
Departure and destination airports must be operational and meet performance requirements

subsections.summary: Establishes a four-level hierarchy for operational decision-making based on the severity and nature of the situation.
key_points: Level 1 – Routine Operations: Handled by operational personnel (e.g., gate changes, minor delays, passenger accommodations)
Level 2 – Operational Disruptions: Handled by supervisors (e.g., significant delays, equipment failures, crew shortages)
Level 3 – Major Disruptions: Handled by OCC management (e.g., airport closures, severe weather, aircraft grounding)
Level 4 – Crisis Events: Handled by executive management (e.g., major accidents, security incidents, national emergencies)

subsections.summary: Establishes rules for version control, review, approval, and distribution of operational procedures.
key_points: All procedures must be version controlled, reviewed annually, approved before publication, and distributed to affected personnel
Personnel shall use only the latest approved version
Outdated documents shall be archived and removed from operational use

subsections.summary: Specifies the categories of operational records that must be maintained and the requirement to retain them per regulatory standards.
key_points: Flight Records: Flight plans, dispatch releases, fuel documentation, delay reports
Crew Records: Qualifications, training records, duty logs
Maintenance Records: Defect reports, maintenance actions, airworthiness documentation
Safety Records: Hazard reports, incident reports, investigation reports
Records shall be retained according to regulatory requirements

subsections.summary: Defines conditions requiring immediate escalation and the process to be followed.
key_points: Personnel must immediately escalate safety concerns, regulatory violations, security incidents, operational emergencies, and significant service disruptions
Escalation shall occur through the established chain of command

subsections.summary: Defines the five-step process that must be followed before implementing operational changes.
key_points: 1. Conduct risk assessment
2. Identify affected stakeholders
3. Update documentation
4. Train affected personnel
5. Monitor implementation results

sections.section_summary: Begins coverage of passenger service operations, focusing on the safe, efficient, secure, and customer-focused movement of passengers from check-in through arrival. The manual continues beyond page 12 with additional subsections on check-in, boarding, baggage, and ground operations.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of Passenger Services and Airport Operations as ensuring safe, efficient, secure, and customer-focused movement of passengers throughout their journey.
key_points: Personnel shall provide professional assistance while maintaining compliance with operational, safety, security, and regulatory requirements
All passenger interactions shall prioritize safety, accuracy, efficiency, and customer satisfaction

subsections.summary: Describes the responsibilities of Passenger Services personnel in managing all stages of the passenger journey, with attention to privacy and data protection.
key_points: Stages include: reservation support, check-in, document verification, baggage acceptance, security coordination, boarding, arrival assistance, connection support, and disruption management
Passenger information shall be handled in accordance with applicable privacy and data protection requirements

subsections.summary: Defines the role of check-in operations in verifying passenger eligibility for travel and ensuring accurate flight documentation, with a detailed list of check-in agent duties.
key_points: Verify passenger identity, travel documentation, and reservation status
Assign seating, process baggage, and issue boarding passes
Identify special service requirements
Passengers shall not be accepted for travel if required travel documents are missing, expired, invalid, or otherwise non-compliant

sections.section_summary: This section continues with detailed passenger service procedures covering document verification, baggage handling, special assistance, boarding operations, delay management, and performance monitoring.

subsections.summary: Procedures for verifying passenger documentation before issuing boarding passes for both domestic and international travel.
key_points: Domestic travel requires government-issued ID, reservation details, and security requirements
International travel requires passport validity, visa, transit, health, and immigration documentation
Travel eligibility uncertainties must be escalated to a supervisor

subsections.summary: Guidelines for managing seat assignments based on multiple operational and passenger criteria.
key_points: Assignments based on aircraft configuration, passenger preferences, safety, special assistance, and operational considerations
Emergency exit row seating restricted to eligible passengers only
Passengers requiring special assistance cannot be assigned to emergency exit row seats

subsections.summary: Requirements for accepting checked baggage, including verification and tagging procedures.
key_points: Baggage accepted only after passenger, flight, weight verification, and security screening
Personnel must verify ownership, apply tags, confirm destination coding, and identify special baggage
Excess baggage fees collected according to company policy

subsections.summary: Identification and handling requirements for special categories of baggage.
key_points: Includes sporting equipment, musical instruments, medical devices, mobility aids, oversized, and fragile items
Special baggage must be tagged and processed according to handling requirements
Passengers advised of applicable limitations or liability restrictions

subsections.summary: Procedures for identifying prohibited and restricted items before baggage acceptance.
key_points: Personnel must identify prohibited items including lithium batteries, flammable materials, explosives, compressed gases, and corrosive substances
Suspected dangerous goods violations must be immediately reported

subsections.summary: Services and coordination requirements for passengers requiring additional support.
key_points: Includes passengers with reduced mobility, elderly, medical conditions, and visual/hearing impairments
Assistance coordinated before departure whenever possible

subsections.summary: Coordination of wheelchair assistance from check-in through arrival at destination.
key_points: Proper documentation of assistance requests required
Equipment availability and safe transport through airport facilities must be ensured
Priority boarding provided where appropriate
Passengers must not be separated from required mobility equipment without approved procedures

subsections.summary: Procedures for accepting and supervising unaccompanied minors during travel.
key_points: Minors accepted only in accordance with company policy
Guardian information must be verified
Required documentation completed and identification materials provided
Child monitored throughout airport processing until transferred to authorized personnel at destination

subsections.summary: Evaluation and handling of passengers requiring medical assistance.
key_points: Requirements may include medical clearance, oxygen arrangements, mobility assistance, and medical equipment approval
Medical information handled confidentially

subsections.summary: Processing standards for VIP passengers while maintaining operational compliance.
key_points: VIPs include government officials, corporate executives, frequent flyers, and special guests
VIP processing conducted professionally without compromising safety, security, or operational requirements
Operational rules apply equally to all passengers

subsections.summary: Personnel responsibilities for supporting airport security procedures.
key_points: Responsibilities include identity verification, boarding pass verification, reporting suspicious activity, and assisting security personnel
Security concerns must be immediately reported

subsections.summary: Standards for conducting boarding operations according to approved schedules.
key_points: Boarding agents verify boarding passes, passenger identity, and security clearance
Passenger flow monitored and boarding status communicated
Boarding conducted in an orderly and efficient manner

subsections.summary: Eligibility and procedures for priority boarding services.
key_points: Provided to passengers requiring assistance, families with young children, premium passengers, and active duty personnel
Priority boarding procedures must not compromise operational efficiency

subsections.summary: Requirements to be completed before gate closure.
key_points: Final passenger counts completed and missing passengers identified
Announcements made and security reconciliation performed
No passenger may board after gate closure without approval

subsections.summary: Reconciliation of boarded passengers against official records.
key_points: Reconciliation performed against passenger manifests, boarding records, and security records
Any discrepancy investigated before departure

subsections.summary: Circumstances and handling of denied boarding situations.
key_points: May occur due to overbooking, documentation deficiencies, security concerns, or operational restrictions
Affected passengers treated professionally and provided assistance per company policy

subsections.summary: Assistance provided to passengers experiencing missed connections.
key_points: Assistance includes rebooking options, accommodation eligibility, meal vouchers, and transportation arrangements
Priority given to minimizing disruption

subsections.summary: Personnel responsibilities during flight delays.
key_points: Provide timely updates and manage passenger expectations
Coordinate support services and escalate passenger concerns
Accurate information must always be provided

subsections.summary: Procedures to follow in the event of flight cancellations.
key_points: Passengers notified promptly and rebooking procedures initiated immediately
Support services coordinated and applicable compensation policies followed

subsections.summary: Coordination of arrival activities and passenger support.
key_points: Passenger disembarkation coordinated
Special assistance passengers receive priority support
Transfer passengers receive guidance and arrival information communicated as necessary

subsections.summary: Standards for handling customer complaints professionally.
key_points: Personnel listen actively, document concerns, provide accurate information, and escalate when required
Complaint trends reviewed to identify improvement opportunities

subsections.summary: Service recovery measures to restore customer confidence.
key_points: May include rebooking assistance, travel credits, meal vouchers, hotel accommodations, and transportation support
Efforts must maintain operational compliance

subsections.summary: Personnel responsibilities for passenger safety throughout operations.
key_points: Support safety announcements, emergency procedures, evacuation readiness, and security compliance
Passenger safety remains the highest priority

subsections.summary: Metrics used to monitor and improve Passenger Services performance.
key_points: Monitoring includes check-in processing times, boarding efficiency, customer satisfaction, complaint trends, operational compliance, and service recovery effectiveness
Performance data reviewed regularly to support continuous improvement

sections.section_summary: This section establishes the purpose, scope, and procedures for check-in operations, which represent the first direct operational interaction between Horizon Airlines and its passengers. Document ID: OPS-CIN-001; Category: Check-In Operations; Priority: High; Version: 1.0.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of Check-In Operations in ensuring passenger eligibility, compliance, and preparation for boarding.
key_points: Verifies passenger eligibility for travel
Ensures compliance with security and regulatory requirements
Processes baggage and issues travel documentation
Plays critical role in schedule integrity, security compliance, and customer satisfaction

subsections.summary: Defines the applicability of check-in procedures across various flight types and check-in channels.
key_points: Applies to all passengers on domestic, international, connecting, charter, code-share, and special operations flights
Covers airport counters, self-service kiosks, online, mobile, and off-airport check-in facilities

subsections.summary: Pre-opening verification and briefing requirements before check-in counters begin operations.
key_points: Verify operational readiness: system, printer, baggage tags, boarding pass stock, manifests, schedules, seat maps, notices
Communication systems verified and operational requirements confirmed
Counter supervisors conduct briefings covering passenger loads, special assistance, disruptions, weather, security alerts, staffing, and flight-specific information

subsections.summary: Requirements for verifying passenger identity before processing check-in.
key_points: Identity verified using approved government-issued documentation
Passenger names must exactly match reservation records
Discrepancies resolved before check-in completion
Acceptable ID includes passports, national ID cards, and other approved travel documentation
Expired or damaged documents evaluated per regulations and airline policy
Suspected fraudulent documentation immediately reported to supervisors and security authorities

subsections.summary: Begins the process of validating passenger reservations against travel requirements.
key_points: Section content continues beyond the provided text

sections.section_summary: Continuation of Check-in Operations covering travel document verification, seat assignments, baggage processing, special passenger handling, and quality assurance procedures. This concludes Section 3 of the operations manual.

subsections.summary: International travel requires verification of all necessary travel documentation including passport validity, visa, transit, health, immigration, and customs requirements. Final admission decisions remain the responsibility of destination authorities.
key_points: Personnel must review passport validity, visa requirements, transit requirements, health documentation, immigration, customs, and destination-specific entry conditions.
Possession of travel documents does not guarantee entry into a country.
Documentation deficiencies must be identified before boarding pass issuance.
Passengers failing destination entry requirements shall not be accepted unless authorized by competent authorities.

subsections.summary: Seat assignments shall be performed using approved reservation systems considering passenger preferences, operational requirements, aircraft balance, accessibility needs, premium entitlements, and safety restrictions.
key_points: Exit row seats may only be assigned to passengers meeting eligibility requirements.
Personnel must verify exit row passengers are physically capable, understand instructions, and meet regulatory requirements.
Passengers requiring special assistance shall not be assigned emergency exit row seats.

subsections.summary: Checked baggage is accepted only after successful passenger verification and reservation validation. Each piece is weighed, inspected, tagged, and entered into tracking systems.
key_points: Personnel must verify baggage ownership, apply destination tags, verify count, and enter baggage into tracking systems.
Excess baggage charges collected when applicable.
Passengers must retain baggage claim receipts until baggage is recovered at destination.

subsections.summary: Personnel must verify compliance with baggage size and weight restrictions, with special handling applied for oversized or overweight baggage.
key_points: Oversized or overweight baggage processed according to approved procedures.
Passengers informed of additional charges, restrictions, or handling limitations.
Baggage exceeding safety limitations not accepted without appropriate authorization.

subsections.summary: Special baggage categories include sporting equipment, musical instruments, medical devices, mobility equipment, fragile items, oversized baggage, and valuable items.
key_points: Personnel apply appropriate handling tags and communicate requirements to baggage operations.
Passengers advised of limitations of liability and handling restrictions.

subsections.summary: All checked and carry-on baggage shall be screened for prohibited and restricted items, with suspected violations reported immediately.
key_points: Items requiring special review include lithium batteries, compressed gases, flammable liquids, explosives, corrosive materials, radioactive substances, and hazardous chemicals.
Suspected violations reported to supervisors and airport security personnel.
No prohibited item accepted without appropriate regulatory approval.

subsections.summary: Passengers requiring special assistance are identified during check-in, with service requirements documented and coordinated throughout the journey.
key_points: Special assistance categories include reduced mobility, elderly, visually impaired, hearing impaired, medical support, and language assistance passengers.
Service requirements communicated to gate and arrival station personnel.

subsections.summary: Unaccompanied minors are processed according to approved procedures with verification of guardian information, emergency contacts, identification, and authorization documentation.
key_points: Required forms completed before acceptance.
Unaccompanied minors remain under continuous supervision until transferred to authorized personnel at destination.
Any deviation from approved procedures requires supervisory approval.

subsections.summary: Passengers requiring medical assistance may need additional review before travel authorization, including evaluation of medical clearances, oxygen, mobility, and equipment needs.
key_points: Confidentiality of medical information maintained at all times.
Medical concerns affecting fitness for travel referred to designated authorities.

subsections.summary: Groups are processed efficiently while maintaining individual passenger verification requirements, with group coordinators providing manifests and documentation in advance.
key_points: Group coordinators provide passenger manifests, travel documentation, baggage information, and special service requirements.
All group members must be accounted for before boarding documentation is issued.

subsections.summary: Passengers arriving after published check-in deadlines may be denied acceptance depending on operational conditions, with evaluation of processing time and security requirements.
key_points: Personnel evaluate processing time, baggage handling limitations, security requirements, and boarding schedules.
Late acceptance must not compromise safety, security, or on-time departure performance.

subsections.summary: Personnel provide timely and accurate information during operational disruptions such as delays, cancellations, gate changes, weather, or security concerns.
key_points: Disruption types include delays, cancellations, gate changes, aircraft substitutions, weather events, maintenance issues, and security concerns.
Passenger communication must remain factual, professional, and consistent with approved operational information.

subsections.summary: Boarding passes are issued only after all eligibility requirements are satisfied and must contain accurate passenger and flight information.
key_points: Boarding passes contain passenger information, seat assignments, flight details, gate information, and boarding sequence.
Errors corrected immediately; lost or damaged passes replaced using approved procedures.

subsections.summary: Check-in operations close according to published schedules, with supervisors verifying passenger counts, baggage reconciliation, standby processing, and special assistance requirements.
key_points: Any unresolved discrepancy escalated before flight departure.
Final passenger information transmitted to gate operations, baggage operations, flight operations, and operational control.

subsections.summary: Check-in performance is monitored through audits, customer feedback, compliance reviews, and operational metrics, with continuous improvement initiatives implemented.
key_points: Monitoring includes operational audits, customer feedback, compliance reviews, baggage processing accuracy, document verification accuracy, security compliance, and departure performance metrics.
Continuous improvement initiatives target efficiency, accuracy, compliance, and passenger satisfaction.

sections.section_summary: Section 4 establishes procedures for the safe, secure, accurate, and efficient transfer of passengers from the terminal to the aircraft. Boarding operations represent the final passenger processing stage before departure and are critical to schedule integrity and operational safety.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of Boarding Operations as ensuring safe, secure, accurate, and efficient transfer of passengers from terminal to aircraft while complying with security, reconciliation, timeline, and safety regulations.
key_points: Boarding procedures ensure compliance with security, passenger reconciliation, operational timelines, and safety regulations.
Minimizes delays while maintaining positive customer experience.
Represents the final passenger processing stage before departure.

subsections.summary: Boarding procedures apply to all scheduled, charter, repositioning, and special operations flights operated by Horizon Airlines, including domestic, international, transit, connecting, charter, and special operations.
key_points: Applies to scheduled, charter, repositioning, and special operations flights.
Covers domestic, international, transit, connecting passengers, charter services, and special operations.
Boarding personnel ensure compliance with operational, security, immigration, customs, and safety requirements.

subsections.summary: Gate personnel verify operational readiness before boarding commences, including aircraft assignment, gate assignment, boarding schedule, passenger manifest, special service requests, operational notices, and security requirements.
key_points: Verification includes aircraft assignment, gate assignment, boarding schedule, passenger manifest, special service requests, operational notices, and security requirements.
Any discrepancy affecting boarding operations immediately escalated.

subsections.summary: Before passenger arrival at the gate, personnel ensure boarding equipment, scanners, announcement systems, and information displays are operational, and that security barriers and emergency exits are properly positioned.
key_points: Boarding equipment, scanners, public announcement systems, and passenger information displays must be operational.
Security barriers properly positioned and emergency exits unobstructed.
Gate areas remain organized and safe throughout boarding.

subsections.summary: Gate personnel review the passenger manifest before boarding begins, including total passenger count, special assistance, unaccompanied minors, VIPs, standby, crew travelers, and security watchlist notifications.
key_points: Manifest review includes passenger count, special assistance, unaccompanied minors, VIPs, standby, crew travelers, and watchlist notifications.
Any discrepancy between manifest data and operational systems resolved before boarding begins.

subsections.summary: Passengers requiring special assistance are identified before boarding, with categories including wheelchair, reduced mobility, medical, elderly, hearing impaired, and visually impaired passengers.
key_points: Special assistance categories include wheelchair, reduced mobility, medical, elderly, hearing impaired, and visually impaired passengers.
Coordination completed with airport assistance personnel before boarding commences.

subsections.summary: Boarding announcements shall provide passengers with clear instructions regarding boarding sequence, gate information, boarding requirements, carry-on baggage restrictions, and final boarding times. Announcements shall be professional, accurate, and timely, with operational changes communicated immediately.
key_points: Must cover boarding sequence, gate info, requirements, baggage restrictions, and final boarding times
Announcements must be professional, accurate, and timely
Operational changes communicated immediately

subsections.summary: Priority boarding may be provided to specific passenger categories and shall be conducted in an orderly manner without compromising security or operational efficiency.
key_points: Eligible passengers: those requiring assistance, unaccompanied minors, families with small children, premium cabin passengers, loyalty program priority passengers, and authorized government personnel
Must be orderly and not compromise security or efficiency

subsections.summary: Boarding shall be conducted according to approved boarding groups organized by various criteria. Personnel shall monitor passenger flow and prevent congestion within boarding areas.
key_points: Boarding groups organized by cabin class, loyalty status, seat location, special assistance requirements, and operational needs
Personnel must monitor flow and prevent congestion

subsections.summary: Every passenger shall present a valid boarding pass before boarding. Personnel must verify multiple elements, and invalid or unauthorized boarding passes shall be investigated immediately. No passenger may board without valid authorization.
key_points: Verify passenger identity, flight number, departure date, boarding authorization, and seat assignment
Invalid, duplicate, altered, or unauthorized passes investigated immediately
No boarding without valid authorization

subsections.summary: Identity verification shall be conducted according to applicable security requirements. Suspected identity fraud shall be immediately escalated to security authorities.
key_points: Passenger identity must match boarding documentation
Travel documents must remain valid
Security requirements must be satisfied
Suspected fraud escalated immediately to security authorities

subsections.summary: Gate personnel shall monitor carry-on baggage compliance with size, weight, and security restrictions. Excess baggage may be transferred to checked baggage processing if necessary.
key_points: Must meet size and weight requirements
Must comply with security restrictions
Excess baggage may be transferred to checked processing
Passengers informed of restrictions before boarding

subsections.summary: Standby passengers shall only be cleared after confirmation of available seating capacity. Standby boarding shall be completed before final boarding closure whenever possible.
key_points: Includes seat assignment, manifest updates, boarding authorization, and passenger notification
Should be completed before final boarding closure

subsections.summary: For overbooked flights, personnel shall follow approved denied boarding procedures, prioritizing voluntary solutions, rebooking options, and customer service recovery measures. Involuntary denied boarding shall be managed according to regulatory requirements and company policy.
key_points: Priority: voluntary solutions, rebooking options, customer service recovery
Involuntary denied boarding per regulatory requirements and company policy

subsections.summary: Passenger reconciliation shall ensure that every boarded passenger is accounted for, with verification of multiple record systems. All discrepancies shall be resolved before departure authorization.
key_points: Verify passenger manifest, boarding records, security records, and special assistance records
All discrepancies resolved before departure authorization

subsections.summary: Passengers who fail to report for boarding before closure shall be classified as no-show passengers. Associated baggage shall be handled according to applicable security procedures.
key_points: Personnel shall attempt passenger contact, verify status, and update operational records
No-show passenger baggage handled per security procedures

subsections.summary: Security reconciliation shall be completed before aircraft departure to ensure all boarded passengers are authorized and records remain consistent. Discrepancies shall be resolved immediately.
key_points: All boarded passengers must be authorized
No unauthorized passenger may have boarded
Passenger and baggage records must remain consistent

subsections.summary: Final boarding announcements shall be made according to operational schedules, identifying remaining passengers, closure deadlines, and consequences of missed boarding. Personnel shall document final boarding activities.
key_points: Identify remaining passengers, boarding closure deadlines, and consequences of missed boarding
Personnel must document final boarding activities

subsections.summary: Gate closure shall occur according to published operational schedules. Multiple verification checks must be completed before closure, and no additional passengers accepted after closure unless authorized by operational control.
key_points: Verify passenger reconciliation, boarding completion, manifest accuracy, and security reconciliation
No additional passengers accepted after gate closure unless authorized

subsections.summary: Gate personnel shall communicate boarding status to flight crew, ground operations, operations control center, and dispatch personnel, including specific operational details.
key_points: Communicate to flight crew, ground operations, operations control center, and dispatch
Information includes passenger count, special assistance status, boarding completion time, and operational concerns

subsections.summary: After boarding completion, personnel shall finalize passenger counts, update manifests, complete boarding reports, and document irregularities. Operational records shall be retained according to company requirements.
key_points: Finalize passenger counts, update manifests, complete boarding reports, document irregularities
Records retained according to company requirements

subsections.summary: If boarding delays occur, personnel shall identify the cause, communicate accurate information, coordinate corrective actions, and escalate significant disruptions. Passengers shall receive timely updates throughout the delay.
key_points: Identify cause, communicate accurate info, coordinate corrective actions, escalate disruptions
Passengers receive timely updates

subsections.summary: Irregular events may include aircraft substitutions, gate changes, security incidents, passenger disturbances, system failures, and weather disruptions. Personnel shall follow approved contingency procedures and maintain continuous communication with operational stakeholders.
key_points: Events include aircraft substitutions, gate changes, security incidents, passenger disturbances, system failures, and weather disruptions
Follow approved contingency procedures with continuous stakeholder communication

subsections.summary: Passengers exhibiting disruptive, aggressive, intoxicated, or threatening behavior shall be evaluated before boarding authorization is granted. Boarding may be denied when necessary to protect safety and security.
key_points: Assess safety risks, notify supervisors, coordinate with security, document all incidents
Boarding may be denied to protect safety and security

subsections.summary: Boarding performance shall be monitored through various metrics, and continuous improvement activities shall be implemented to enhance efficiency, compliance, safety, and customer experience.
key_points: Monitor boarding completion times, on-time departure performance, reconciliation accuracy, security compliance, customer satisfaction, and incident reporting trends
Continuous improvement for efficiency, compliance, safety, and customer experience

sections.section_summary: This section establishes procedures for the safe, secure, accurate, and timely movement of passenger baggage from acceptance through delivery, supporting operational efficiency, passenger satisfaction, security compliance, and aircraft loading requirements.

subsections.summary: The purpose of Baggage Handling Operations is to ensure the safe, secure, accurate, and timely movement of passenger baggage from acceptance through delivery. All baggage shall be processed in accordance with safety regulations, security requirements, and company procedures.
key_points: Ensure safe, secure, accurate, and timely baggage movement
Support operational efficiency, passenger satisfaction, security compliance, and aircraft loading requirements
Reference sources: FAA Airport Operations Handbook, IATA Airport Handling Practices, Flight Operations Manual Template, UK OTAC Operations Manual Guidance

subsections.summary: These procedures apply to all checked baggage, transfer baggage, special baggage, oversized baggage, crew baggage, delayed baggage, and mishandled baggage processed by Horizon Airlines. Baggage handling personnel shall maintain custody and accountability of baggage throughout the transportation process.
key_points: Covers all baggage types: checked, transfer, special, oversized, crew, delayed, and mishandled
Personnel must maintain custody and accountability throughout transportation

subsections.summary: Baggage acceptance begins during passenger check-in. Personnel shall verify baggage ownership before accepting baggage for transport. Each accepted bag shall receive a valid baggage tag with destination, flight details, and unique tracking identifiers. Only ticketed passengers with confirmed travel authorization may have baggage accepted.
key_points: Verify baggage ownership before acceptance
Each bag receives a valid tag with destination, flight, and tracking identifiers
Only accepted from ticketed passengers with confirmed travel authorization
Improperly tagged baggage removed from processing until discrepancies resolved

subsections.summary: Each baggage item shall be assigned a unique baggage identification number recorded within approved baggage tracking systems. Personnel shall verify that tag information matches passenger reservation records and flight routing. Incorrect tagging may result in delays, security concerns, and operational disruptions and shall be corrected immediately.
key_points: Unique identification number assigned to each item
Information recorded in approved baggage tracking systems
Tag information must match passenger reservation and flight routing
Incorrect tagging corrected immediately

subsections.summary: All baggage shall undergo required security screening before loading, which may include X-ray inspection, explosive detection screening, manual inspection, or additional procedures. Baggage failing security requirements shall not proceed until clearance is obtained, and suspicious items shall be immediately reported.
key_points: Screening methods: X-ray, explosive detection, manual inspection, or additional local procedures
Failed baggage held until clearance obtained
Suspicious items reported immediately to airport security and supervisors

subsections.summary: Following acceptance and screening, baggage shall be sorted according to destination, flight number, transfer routing, and handling requirements. Sorting personnel shall verify multiple sorting criteria, and incorrectly sorted baggage shall be immediately corrected.
key_points: Verify flight assignment, destination coding, priority status, transfer status, and special handling
Incorrectly sorted baggage corrected immediately

subsections.summary: Transfer baggage refers to baggage continuing onto a connecting flight. Transfer baggage personnel shall verify onward flight information, confirm routing, ensure transfer deadlines are met, and coordinate with connecting stations. Priority shall be given to short connection baggage to minimize transfer failures.
key_points: Verify onward flight information, confirm routing, meet transfer deadlines, coordinate with stations
Priority given to short connection baggage

subsections.summary: Priority baggage includes premium cabin baggage, frequent flyer priority baggage, crew baggage, and operational priority baggage. Priority baggage shall receive expedited handling and loading, with procedures monitored to maintain service standards.
key_points: Includes premium cabin, frequent flyer priority, crew, and operational priority baggage
Receives expedited handling and loading
Procedures monitored to maintain service standards

subsections.summary: Special baggage may include sporting equipment, musical instruments, medical equipment, mobility aids, fragile items, and oversized items. Personnel shall apply appropriate handling tags and ensure special handling instructions accompany the baggage throughout processing.
key_points: Categories: sporting equipment, musical instruments, medical equipment, mobility aids, fragile items, oversized items
Appropriate handling tags required
Special handling instructions must accompany baggage
Protected from unnecessary damage or mishandling

subsections.summary: Oversized baggage shall be processed separately from standard baggage streams. Personnel shall verify weight limitations, dimensional limitations, aircraft compatibility, and loading requirements. Manual handling shall use approved lifting procedures.
key_points: Processed separately from standard baggage
Verify weight, dimensions, aircraft compatibility, and loading requirements
Manual handling uses approved lifting procedures

subsections.summary: Fragile baggage shall be identified and tagged appropriately. Examples include musical instruments, electronic equipment, artwork, and glass items. Personnel shall exercise additional care during transportation and loading. Fragile tags indicate special handling requirements but do not eliminate damage risk.
key_points: Examples: musical instruments, electronic equipment, artwork, glass items
Additional care during transportation and loading
Fragile tags indicate special handling but do not eliminate damage risk

subsections.summary: Wheelchairs and mobility devices shall receive special handling, including condition recording, component protection, proper securing, and prioritized delivery upon arrival.
key_points: Record condition before loading
Protect sensitive components
Secure equipment properly
Prioritize delivery upon arrival

sections.section_summary: This section concludes the baggage handling operations procedures, covering aircraft baggage loading, weight and balance coordination, safety procedures, reconciliation, delivery, delayed/lost/damaged baggage handling, tracking systems, and continuous improvement. [Page 42-47]

subsections.summary: Personnel shall review aircraft loading instructions before loading baggage, ensuring compliance with weight and balance, load control, compartment limitations, and special handling requirements.
key_points: Review loading instructions before operations
Comply with weight and balance requirements
Follow load control and compartment limitations
Improper loading may affect aircraft performance

subsections.summary: Baggage loading shall support aircraft weight and balance requirements through coordination with load control personnel. Discrepancies must be reported immediately, and loading shall not proceed until corrected instructions are received.
key_points: Coordinate with load control personnel
Report balance discrepancies immediately
Loading shall not proceed until corrections received

subsections.summary: Personnel shall follow safe loading practices at all times, including proper lifting techniques, use of approved equipment, compliance with ramp safety rules, and awareness of moving vehicles.
key_points: Use proper lifting techniques
Use approved equipment only
Comply with ramp safety rules
Report unsafe conditions immediately

subsections.summary: Before departure, baggage reconciliation shall confirm loaded baggage corresponds to accepted passengers by verifying passenger status, baggage counts, security requirements, and loading records.
key_points: Verify passenger status and baggage counts
Confirm security requirements met
Resolve discrepancies before departure authorization

subsections.summary: If a passenger fails to board, associated baggage shall be identified and handled per security requirements, including locating baggage, verifying requirements, removing if needed, and updating records.
key_points: Locate and verify affected baggage
Remove baggage if security requires
Update operational records
Complete procedures before departure

subsections.summary: Upon aircraft arrival, baggage shall be unloaded according to approved procedures, prioritizing mobility aids, priority baggage, transfer baggage, and standard baggage, then transported to designated delivery areas.
key_points: Prioritize mobility aids and priority baggage
Handle transfer and standard baggage
Transport promptly to delivery areas

subsections.summary: Baggage shall be delivered to passengers quickly and accurately, ensuring correct destination delivery, accurate carousel assignment, and timely passenger communication while minimizing delays.
key_points: Ensure correct destination delivery
Assign accurate carousel locations
Minimize delivery delays

subsections.summary: Delayed baggage occurs when baggage does not arrive on the same flight as the passenger. Personnel shall create irregularity reports, verify passenger information, initiate tracing, and provide updates.
key_points: Create baggage irregularity report
Initiate baggage tracing
Provide regular passenger updates
Reunite baggage with owner promptly

subsections.summary: Baggage may be classified as lost when recovery efforts fail within established timelines. Personnel shall conduct tracing investigations, review records, coordinate with partner stations, and maintain passenger communication.
key_points: Conduct tracing investigations
Coordinate with partner stations
Follow compensation regulations and company policy

subsections.summary: Passengers reporting baggage damage shall receive prompt assistance. Personnel shall inspect damage, document findings, create incident reports, and determine compensation eligibility.
key_points: Inspect and document reported damage
Create incident reports
Determine compensation eligibility

subsections.summary: Unclaimed baggage shall be transferred to designated storage facilities. Personnel shall verify ownership, attempt passenger contact, and maintain storage records per regulatory and company requirements.
key_points: Transfer to designated storage facilities
Verify ownership and contact passengers
Maintain storage records

subsections.summary: Documentable events include lost, delayed, damaged, mishandled baggage, security incidents, and tracking failures. Reports shall be reviewed to identify recurring operational issues.
key_points: Document all baggage incidents
Include security incidents and tracking failures
Review reports for recurring issues

subsections.summary: Approved baggage tracking systems shall monitor baggage throughout its journey, supporting acceptance, routing, loading, arrival records, and delivery confirmation. Discrepancies shall be investigated immediately.
key_points: Use approved tracking systems
Support all journey stages
Investigate system discrepancies immediately

subsections.summary: Baggage handling performance shall be monitored using mishandled rates, delivery times, damage rates, transfer success, security compliance, and complaint trends to support continuous improvement.
key_points: Monitor mishandled baggage rates
Track delivery times and damage rates
Review passenger complaint trends

subsections.summary: Baggage handling operations shall be continuously reviewed to improve safety, efficiency, reliability, and customer satisfaction through operational audits, employee feedback, incident investigations, and performance data.
key_points: Conduct operational audits
Use employee feedback and incident investigations
Identify improvement and corrective action opportunities

sections.section_title: Section 6 – Ground Operations & Aircraft Turnaround Operations
sections.section_summary: This section establishes procedures for safe, secure, efficient, and timely handling of aircraft while on the ground, covering aircraft arrival, parking, disembarkation, servicing, cleaning, fueling, and turnaround operations. [Page 47-51]

subsections.summary: The purpose is to ensure safe, secure, efficient, and timely handling of aircraft while on the ground, encompassing all activities from arrival at parking position through departure, in compliance with approved procedures, safety, security, and manufacturer guidance.
key_points: Ensure safe and secure ground handling
Coordinate turnaround operations
Comply with operational and safety requirements

subsections.summary: Ground operations include arrival handling, marshalling, parking, disembarkation support, baggage coordination, catering, fueling, cabin servicing, cleaning, maintenance, cargo, pushback, and departure preparation, applying to all Horizon Airlines aircraft and contracted personnel.
key_points: Covers all ground handling activities
Applies to all Horizon Airlines aircraft
Includes contracted ground handling personnel

subsections.summary: Prior to arrival, personnel shall verify gate readiness, equipment, staffing, and safety areas. Parking stands shall be inspected for FOD, obstructions, and contamination. Marshalling personnel shall guide aircraft to parking using approved signals or docking systems.
key_points: Verify gate readiness and equipment availability
Inspect parking stands for hazards
Monitor aircraft movement for safe clearance

subsections.summary: After parking, wheel chocks shall be installed per approved procedures, engine shutdown confirmed, and safety cones positioned around hazard areas. Personnel shall not approach until authorization is provided and safety conditions are met.
key_points: Install wheel chocks per approved procedures
Confirm engine shutdown before approach
Position safety cones around hazard areas

subsections.summary: Ground safety zones shall be established around parked aircraft, including engine danger zones, propeller hazards, jet blast zones, fueling zones, and movement paths. Personnel shall remain aware of operating aircraft, vehicles, fueling, and weather.
key_points: Establish restricted areas around aircraft
Personnel awareness of engines, vehicles, fueling
Unauthorized personnel prohibited from restricted areas

subsections.summary: Following arrival, disembarkation equipment shall be positioned safely, with jet bridges, stairs, and mobility equipment inspected prior to use. Personnel shall coordinate with cabin crew, provide priority assistance, and maintain security.
key_points: Inspect equipment before use
Coordinate with cabin crew
Provide priority support to passengers requiring assistance

subsections.summary: GSE includes passenger stairs, belt loaders, pushback tractors, ground power units, air conditioning units, baggage carts, tow bars, and service vehicles. Equipment shall be inspected before use and defective items removed from service.
key_points: Includes stairs, belt loaders, pushback tractors, GPUs, ACUs
Inspect equipment before use
Remove defective equipment from service immediately

subsections.summary: Unloading shall begin only after safety procedures are completed, following approved loading plans. Priority baggage, mobility aids, transfer, and special baggage shall receive expedited processing while protecting from damage.
key_points: Begin only after safety procedures complete
Prioritize mobility aids and special baggage
Protect baggage from damage during transfer

subsections.summary: Cargo and mail shall be unloaded, transferred, and loaded per approved procedures. Personnel shall verify documentation, handling requirements, security status, and destination. Special cargo shall be handled per applicable regulations.
key_points: Verify shipment documentation and security status
Handle special cargo per applicable regulations
Confirm destination and handling requirements

subsections.summary: Cleaning shall begin after disembarkation and safety clearance. Personnel shall remove waste, clean seating and lavatories, replenish supplies, and inspect cabin condition within scheduled turnaround timelines.
key_points: Remove waste and clean cabin areas
Replenish cabin supplies
Complete within scheduled turnaround timelines

subsections.summary: Aircraft servicing may include potable water replenishment and lavatory waste servicing. Personnel shall use approved equipment, follow hygiene requirements, prevent contamination, and document completion per environmental and health regulations.
key_points: Use approved servicing equipment
Follow hygiene and contamination prevention
Comply with environmental and health regulations

subsections.summary: Catering personnel shall coordinate delivery and loading of food, beverages, and supplies, including removal of used supplies, loading required inventory, verifying quantities, and documenting services while maintaining food safety standards.
key_points: Remove used supplies and load required inventory
Verify catering quantities
Maintain food safety standards throughout

subsections.summary: Aircraft fueling shall only be conducted by authorized personnel. Prior to fueling, aircraft grounding, fire safety, fuel quantities, and communications shall be verified. During fueling, personnel shall continuously monitor for leaks, malfunctions, and hazards.
key_points: Complete aircraft grounding and fire safety verification
Confirm fuel quantities and communications
Continuously monitor fueling for leaks and hazards

sections.section_title: Section 6 – Ground Operations & Aircraft Turnaround Operations (Continued)
sections.section_summary: This section continues the ground operations procedures, covering maintenance coordination, servicing coordination, departure preparation, load control, walkaround inspection, pushback, performance monitoring, irregular operations, and continuous improvement.

subsections.summary: Maintenance personnel evaluate aircraft defects, scheduled maintenance, and operational limitations during turnaround. Maintenance actions include technical inspections, component replacement, system testing, and defect rectification, coordinated to minimize disruption while maintaining airworthiness.
key_points: Evaluate reported defects and maintenance requirements
Maintenance actions include inspections, component replacement, system testing, defect rectification
Activities coordinated to minimize operational disruption

subsections.summary: Turnaround coordinators monitor all servicing activities to ensure timely completion. Servicing activities include fueling, catering, cleaning, baggage loading, cargo loading, and maintenance support, with delays communicated immediately to operational control.
key_points: Monitor fueling, catering, cleaning, baggage, cargo, and maintenance activities
Ensure completion within scheduled timelines
Communicate potential delays immediately

subsections.summary: Personnel verify completion of all turnaround activities prior to departure, including boarding status, baggage, cargo, fueling, maintenance release, and documentation. Unresolved issues are escalated before departure authorization.
key_points: Verify passenger boarding, baggage, cargo, fueling, maintenance release, and documentation
Escalate any unresolved issues before departure authorization

subsections.summary: Ground operations personnel coordinate with load control to ensure aircraft loading complies with weight and balance requirements. Discrepancies affecting balance, structural limitations, or safety must be reported immediately.
key_points: Ensure compliance with weight and balance requirements
Follow loading instructions precisely
Report any safety-affecting discrepancies immediately

subsections.summary: Designated personnel conduct a final walkaround inspection before departure to verify equipment removal, cargo and baggage door security, absence of leaks and foreign object debris, and aircraft exterior condition. Abnormal conditions must be investigated.
key_points: Verify equipment removal and door/baggage compartment security
Check for leaks, FOD, and exterior condition
Investigate any abnormal conditions before departure

subsections.summary: Before pushback, personnel verify passenger boarding completion, door closure, equipment removal, pushback route clearance, and communication with flight crew. Pushback only commences after required authorization.
key_points: Verify boarding, door closure, equipment removal, route clearance, crew communication
Pushback requires proper authorization before commencement

subsections.summary: Pushback is performed by trained personnel using approved equipment and procedures with continuous communication between pushback personnel and flight crew. Any abnormal condition results in immediate suspension.
key_points: Performed by trained personnel using approved equipment
Continuous communication with flight crew required
Abnormal conditions cause immediate suspension

subsections.summary: Turnaround performance is monitored through on-time departure, ground delay statistics, safety indicators, equipment reliability, and service quality. Data is reviewed regularly to identify improvement opportunities.
key_points: Monitor on-time performance, delays, safety, equipment reliability, service quality
Data reviewed regularly for improvement opportunities

subsections.summary: Irregular events include equipment failures, weather disruptions, fueling delays, maintenance delays, passenger disruptions, and security incidents. Personnel follow contingency procedures and coordinate corrective actions.
key_points: Irregular events include equipment, weather, fueling, maintenance, passenger, security issues
Follow approved contingency procedures
Coordinate corrective actions to minimize impact

subsections.summary: Ground operations and turnaround procedures are reviewed periodically through audits, inspections, safety reviews, operational analysis, and performance monitoring. Lessons learned are incorporated into future procedures.
key_points: Periodic reviews via audits, inspections, safety reviews, and analysis
Incorporate lessons learned into future procedures

sections.section_summary: This section defines the purpose, scope, and procedures for flight dispatch and planning, ensuring every flight is planned, authorized, and monitored in accordance with regulatory requirements and safety standards.

subsections.summary: The purpose of Dispatch and Flight Planning Operations is to ensure every flight is planned, authorized, monitored, and supported in accordance with regulatory requirements, operational limitations, safety standards, and company policies. Dispatch personnel evaluate conditions, assess risks, coordinate resources, and provide crews with required information.
key_points: Ensure flights comply with regulations and safety standards
Dispatchers evaluate conditions, assess risks, coordinate resources
Provide flight crews with required operational information

subsections.summary: Dispatch responsibilities include flight planning, route analysis, fuel planning, weather assessment, airport suitability review, NOTAM analysis, operational risk assessment, flight release preparation, operational monitoring, and coordination with stakeholders.
key_points: Includes planning, route analysis, fuel, weather, NOTAMs, risk assessment
Dispatch serves as primary operational planning authority before departure

subsections.summary: Dispatch personnel review flight schedules, aircraft assignments, crew assignments, airport operating hours, slot restrictions, and operational notices prior to flight planning. Operational conflicts are identified and resolved before flight release.
key_points: Review schedules, assignments, operating hours, slot restrictions, notices
Resolve operational conflicts before flight release

subsections.summary: Routes are selected based on operational efficiency, air traffic restrictions, weather, fuel efficiency, airspace availability, and regulatory requirements. Routes comply with approved navigation procedures.
key_points: Select routes based on efficiency, traffic, weather, fuel, airspace, regulations
Routes must comply with approved navigation procedures

subsections.summary: Weather assessments include departure, destination, alternate airport conditions, enroute weather, convective activity, turbulence, wind, and visibility. Weather information is continuously monitored.
key_points: Assess weather at departure, destination, alternates, and enroute
Monitor convective activity, turbulence, wind, visibility
Continuously monitor during planning process

subsections.summary: Dispatch personnel review all applicable Notices to Air Missions (NOTAMs) for runway closures, taxiway closures, navigation aid outages, airport construction, airspace restrictions, and temporary procedures. Operational impacts are assessed before flight release.
key_points: Review NOTAMs for closures, outages, construction, restrictions
Assess operational impacts before flight release

subsections.summary: Aircraft performance calculations consider aircraft type, weight, runway conditions, temperature, elevation, wind, and operational restrictions. Dispatch ensures the aircraft can safely operate within all performance limitations.
key_points: Consider type, weight, runway, temperature, elevation, wind, restrictions
Ensure safe operation within performance limitations

subsections.summary: Fuel planning ensures sufficient fuel for taxi, trip, contingency, alternate, holding, and regulatory reserves. Additional fuel may be authorized when operational conditions indicate increased risk.
key_points: Cover taxi, trip, contingency, alternate, holding, regulatory reserves
Additional fuel permitted for higher-risk conditions

subsections.summary: Suitable alternate airports are selected based on weather suitability, runway capability, operational status, aircraft compatibility, and fuel requirements. Alternates remain available throughout the planned operation.
key_points: Select based on weather, runway, status, aircraft compatibility, fuel
Alternates must remain available throughout operation

subsections.summary: Dispatch personnel prepare a flight release containing flight routing, fuel requirements, weather, NOTAMs, operational restrictions, and aircraft information. The release serves as official authorization for flight operations.
key_points: Release includes routing, fuel, weather, NOTAMs, restrictions, aircraft info
Serves as official authorization for flight

subsections.summary: Flight crews receive all operationally significant information before departure, including weather concerns, fuel considerations, airport restrictions, aircraft limitations, and operational risks. Questions and concerns are addressed before departure authorization.
key_points: Brief crews on weather, fuel, restrictions, limitations, risks
Address concerns before departure authorization

subsections.summary: Dispatch personnel evaluate risks associated with weather, maintenance limitations, airport conditions, crew limitations, security concerns, and airspace restrictions. Risk mitigation measures are implemented when necessary.
key_points: Evaluate risks across weather, maintenance, airports, crew, security, airspace
Implement mitigation measures as needed

subsections.summary: Prior to departure, dispatch monitors aircraft readiness, crew readiness, weather developments, airport conditions, fuel status, and maintenance status. Significant changes trigger reassessment of operational suitability.
key_points: Monitor aircraft, crew, weather, airports, fuel, maintenance
Significant changes require reassessment

subsections.summary: After departure, dispatch continues monitoring flight progress, weather, airspace restrictions, fuel consumption, and operational deviations. Operational support is provided throughout the flight.
key_points: Monitor progress, weather, airspace, fuel, deviations enroute
Provide continuous operational support

subsections.summary: If a diversion becomes necessary, dispatch identifies suitable diversion airports, evaluates operational conditions, coordinates ground support, and provides information to flight crews. Diversion decisions prioritize safety.
key_points: Identify diversion airports and evaluate conditions
Coordinate ground support and inform crews
Safety is the priority in diversion decisions

subsections.summary: Dispatch coordinates responses to delays, diversions, cancellations, aircraft substitutions, airport closures, and weather disruptions. Operational recovery plans are developed to minimize disruption.
key_points: Coordinate responses to delays, diversions, cancellations, substitutions, closures
Develop recovery plans to minimize disruption

subsections.summary: Following flight completion, dispatch reviews operational performance, fuel performance, weather impacts, delays, and operational deviations. Lessons learned are incorporated into future planning.
key_points: Review performance, fuel, weather, delays, deviations
Incorporate lessons learned into future planning

subsections.summary: Dispatch performance is monitored through on-time performance, fuel efficiency, diversion rates, delay statistics, regulatory compliance, and operational safety indicators.
key_points: Track on-time, fuel efficiency, diversion, delays, compliance, safety

sections.section_summary: This section defines the OCC's role as the central command and coordination facility responsible for maintaining operational awareness, real-time monitoring, decision-making, communication, disruption management, and operational recovery across the airline network.

subsections.summary: The Operations Control Center (OCC) serves as the central command and coordination facility responsible for maintaining operational awareness and ensuring the safe, efficient, and continuous execution of airline operations. It provides real-time monitoring, decision-making, communication, disruption management, and operational recovery support.
key_points: Central command and coordination facility for airline operations
Provides real-time monitoring, decision-making, and communication
Manages disruptions and supports operational recovery

subsections.summary: The OCC is responsible for flight monitoring, network monitoring, operational recovery, resource coordination, crew coordination, aircraft utilization, disruption management, and emergency coordination, maintaining oversight of all active airline operations.
key_points: Covers flight, network, resources, crew, aircraft, disruption, emergency coordination
Maintains oversight of all active operations

subsections.summary: The OCC may consist of an OCC Manager, Flight Operations Coordinators, Dispatch Personnel, Crew Controllers, Maintenance Controllers, Network Controllers, and Operational Support Specialists. Each role contributes to operational continuity and situational awareness.
key_points: Includes Manager, Coordinators, Dispatchers, Crew/Maintenance/Network Controllers, Support Specialists
Each role supports operational continuity and situational awareness

subsections.summary: The OCC continuously monitors aircraft locations, flight status, airport conditions, weather, crew status, maintenance status, passenger disruptions, and security concerns. Operational information is updated in real time whenever possible.
key_points: Monitor aircraft, flight, airport, weather, crew, maintenance, passenger, security
Update operational information in real time

sections.section_summary: The final subsections of Maintenance Coordination address defect evaluation, maintenance planning, control, deferred defect management, aircraft release to service, technical communications, unscheduled maintenance events, and performance monitoring.

subsections.summary: Reported defects are assessed for safety impact, operational impact, repair requirements, and dispatch limitations. Defects affecting airworthiness must be addressed before further operation.
key_points: Defects must be assessed for safety and operational impact
Repair requirements and dispatch limitations must be determined
Airworthiness-affecting defects must be addressed before further operation

subsections.summary: Maintenance planning ensures required work is completed within approved intervals, including scheduled maintenance, inspections, component replacements, and engineering modifications.
key_points: Planning covers scheduled maintenance, inspections, component replacements, and engineering modifications
Schedules must be coordinated with operational requirements

subsections.summary: Maintenance Control monitors fleet airworthiness, defect status, maintenance progress, and aircraft availability, and communicates significant technical issues to operational stakeholders.
key_points: Monitors fleet airworthiness, defect status, maintenance progress, and aircraft availability
Communicates significant technical issues to operational stakeholders

subsections.summary: Certain defects may be deferred in accordance with approved procedures, provided they are documented, monitored, comply with approved limitations, and are corrected within required timelines.
key_points: Deferred defects must be documented and monitored
Must comply with approved limitations and corrected within required timelines

subsections.summary: Before aircraft release, maintenance personnel verify required maintenance completion, documentation accuracy, airworthiness status, and operational suitability. Release authority is exercised only by authorized personnel.
key_points: Verifies maintenance completion, documentation accuracy, airworthiness status, and operational suitability
Release authority is limited to authorized personnel

subsections.summary: Maintenance personnel maintain communication with flight crews, OCC personnel, dispatch personnel, and engineering personnel to support safe operational decision-making.
key_points: Communication maintained with flight crews, OCC, dispatch, and engineering personnel
Timely communication supports safe operational decision-making

subsections.summary: Unscheduled maintenance may result from technical failures, inspection findings, operational reports, or component malfunctions. Operational impacts must be assessed and communicated promptly.
key_points: May result from technical failures, inspection findings, operational reports, or component malfunctions
Operational impacts must be assessed and communicated promptly

subsections.summary: Maintenance performance is monitored through aircraft reliability, defect rates, maintenance delays, technical dispatch reliability, and airworthiness compliance to support continuous improvement.
key_points: Monitored through aircraft reliability, defect rates, maintenance delays, technical dispatch reliability, and airworthiness compliance
Performance data supports continuous improvement initiatives

sections.section_summary: Security Operations procedures protect passengers, crew, aircraft, facilities, information systems, cargo, baggage, and operational assets from unlawful interference, security threats, criminal activity, sabotage, terrorism, and unauthorized access.

subsections.summary: The purpose of Security Operations is to protect passengers, crew, aircraft, facilities, information systems, cargo, baggage, and operational assets from unlawful interference, threats, criminal activity, sabotage, terrorism, and unauthorized access. Procedures shall be integrated into all operational activities.
key_points: Protects people, assets, and systems from unlawful interference and threats
Procedures integrated with airport authorities, law enforcement, regulators, and operational departments

subsections.summary: Access to operational areas is restricted to authorized personnel who must display valid identification, present airport access credentials, comply with screening requirements, and follow escort requirements when applicable.
key_points: Access restricted to authorized personnel only
Requires valid ID, credentials, screening, and escort compliance
Unauthorized individuals shall be denied access and reported

subsections.summary: Restricted areas include aircraft parking stands, ramp areas, baggage facilities, cargo facilities, maintenance facilities, and OCC facilities. Personnel shall continuously monitor for suspicious activity and unauthorized access.
key_points: Covers aircraft parking, ramps, baggage, cargo, maintenance, and OCC facilities
Continuous monitoring for suspicious activity, unauthorized access, and unattended items

subsections.summary: Aircraft security inspections are conducted before first flight, after extended ground periods, following security incidents, or when directed by authorities. Inspections cover cabins, lavatories, galleys, cargo compartments, flight deck, and service compartments.
key_points: Conducted before first flight, after extended ground periods, or following incidents
Covers cabin, lavatories, galleys, cargo compartments, flight deck, and service compartments
Suspicious items result in immediate suspension of operations

subsections.summary: Personnel identifying suspicious individuals should observe behavior, avoid confrontation, notify supervisors and security personnel, and document observations. Indicators include unauthorized access, surveillance, unusual photography, threatening behavior, and identity discrepancies.
key_points: Steps include observation, non-confrontation, notification, and documentation
Indicators include unauthorized access attempts, surveillance, unusual photography, and identity discrepancies

subsections.summary: Any unattended item shall be treated as potentially hazardous. Personnel shall establish a safety perimeter, prevent public access, notify security, document location and time, and await instructions without touching or moving items.
key_points: All unattended items treated as potentially hazardous
Personnel must not touch or move suspicious items
Establish safety perimeter and notify security

subsections.summary: Upon receiving a bomb threat, personnel shall remain calm, record information, and notify OCC, airport security, and law enforcement. Operations may be suspended and facilities evacuated pending security assessment.
key_points: Remain calm, record information, notify OCC, airport security, and law enforcement
Operations may be suspended and facilities evacuated

subsections.summary: Passengers may be denied travel due to threatening behavior, violence, intoxication, security concerns, or identity discrepancies. Security personnel coordinate with operational personnel to ensure safe resolution.
key_points: Denial grounds include threatening behavior, violence, intoxication, security concerns, and identity discrepancies
Coordination between security and operational personnel required

subsections.summary: All security incidents shall be documented with time, location, personnel involved, description, actions taken, and outcome. Reports shall be retained according to regulatory requirements.
key_points: Reports must include time, location, personnel, description, actions, and outcome
Reports retained per regulatory requirements

subsections.summary: Personnel shall protect operational systems from unauthorized access through password protection, access controls, system monitoring, and incident reporting. Suspected cybersecurity incidents must be reported immediately.
key_points: Measures include password protection, access controls, system monitoring, and incident reporting
Suspected incidents reported immediately

subsections.summary: Security audits evaluate access control effectiveness, security compliance, incident trends, and procedural effectiveness. Corrective actions shall be tracked until completion.
key_points: Evaluates access control, compliance, incident trends, and procedural effectiveness
Corrective actions tracked until completion

sections.section_summary: Weather Disruption Management procedures ensure safe airline operations during adverse meteorological conditions. All weather-related decisions prioritize safety over schedule performance and address impacts on flight safety, airport operations, aircraft performance, crew scheduling, and network stability.
