subsections.summary: The purpose of Weather Disruption Management is to ensure safe airline operations during adverse meteorological conditions. Weather disruptions may affect flight safety, airport operations, aircraft performance, crew scheduling, passenger handling, and network stability.
key_points: Ensures safe operations during adverse weather
Safety prioritized over schedule performance

subsections.summary: The OCC continuously monitors departure, destination, alternate, and enroute weather, including tropical systems, thunderstorms, low visibility, and wind conditions throughout operational periods.
key_points: Monitors departure, destination, alternate, and enroute weather
Covers tropical systems, thunderstorms, low visibility, and wind conditions

subsections.summary: When significant weather is forecast, OCC issues alerts, dispatch reviews affected flights, crew scheduling evaluates impacts, ground operations prepares contingencies, and passenger services prepares communication plans.
key_points: OCC issues operational alerts for forecast significant weather
Coordinated response across dispatch, crew scheduling, ground ops, and passenger services
Alerts remain active until operational risk is reduced

subsections.summary: Thunderstorms present risks including lightning, wind shear, turbulence, heavy rainfall, reduced visibility, and hail. Operations may be modified, restricted, or delayed, with safety overriding schedule performance.
key_points: Risks include lightning, wind shear, turbulence, heavy rain, reduced visibility, and hail
Aircraft routing, ground operations, fuel planning, and departures may be adjusted
Safety considerations override schedule performance

subsections.summary: When lightning is detected within airport safety limits, ramp operations suspend, fueling ceases, aircraft loading stops, and personnel move to designated shelters. Operations resume only after clearance from authorities.
key_points: Ramp operations, fueling, and aircraft loading suspended
Personnel move to designated shelters
Operations resume only after clearance from airport authorities

subsections.summary: Low visibility from fog, heavy rain, smoke, dust, or haze may require additional spacing, taxi restrictions, increased delays, and diversions. Flight crews receive continuous visibility updates.
key_points: Causes include fog, heavy rain, smoke, dust, and haze
May require additional spacing, taxi restrictions, delays, or diversions
Flight crews provided with continuous visibility updates

subsections.summary: Strong winds affect aircraft performance, ground equipment, passenger boarding, and aircraft parking. Personnel shall secure loose equipment and monitor hazards. Aircraft exceeding crosswind limits shall not be dispatched.
key_points: Affects aircraft performance, equipment, boarding, and parking
Personnel must secure loose equipment and monitor hazards
Aircraft exceeding crosswind limits shall not be dispatched

subsections.summary: When tropical systems threaten operational areas, OCC activates disruption planning, aircraft repositioning may be initiated, flight schedules modified, airport closures monitored, and passenger recovery plans prepared.
key_points: OCC activates disruption planning
Aircraft repositioning, schedule modifications, and passenger recovery plans prepared
Aircraft shall not be exposed to unacceptable storm risk

subsections.summary: Snow or ice conditions require deicing assessment, runway monitoring, ground movement restrictions, and additional delays. No aircraft shall depart with contamination exceeding approved limits.
key_points: Aircraft deicing requirements assessed
Runway conditions monitored and ground movement may be restricted
No departure permitted with contamination exceeding approved limits

subsections.summary: Diversion may be required when destination weather falls below minima, runways become unavailable, or safety margins are reduced. Dispatch identifies alternates while OCC coordinates support and passenger services prepares recovery.
key_points: Triggers include destination weather below minima, runway unavailability, or reduced safety margins
Dispatch identifies alternates, OCC coordinates support, ground handling arranged

subsections.summary: If an airport becomes unavailable, affected flights are evaluated, diversion plans activated, passenger notifications begin, and crew recovery planning commences.
key_points: Affected flights evaluated and diversion plans activated
Passenger notifications and crew recovery planning commence
Operational recovery begins immediately

subsections.summary: Following severe weather, aircraft inspections may be required, schedule and passenger recovery plans activated, and operational performance reviewed. Lessons learned are incorporated into future planning.
key_points: Aircraft inspections may be required
Schedule and passenger recovery plans activated
Lessons learned incorporated into future planning

subsections.summary: Weather disruption performance is evaluated through delay statistics, diversion rates, passenger recovery times, operational recovery effectiveness, and safety performance indicators.
key_points: Evaluated through delay statistics, diversion rates, and passenger recovery times
Includes operational recovery effectiveness and safety performance indicators

sections.section_summary: This section addresses Irregular Operations (IROPS) management, including flight delays, diversions, and cancellations. The purpose is to minimize operational disruption, maintain safety, support passengers, and facilitate rapid recovery.

subsections.summary: The purpose of Delay, Diversion, and Cancellation Management is to minimize operational disruption, maintain safety, support passengers, protect operational continuity, and facilitate rapid recovery following irregular operational events.
key_points: Minimizes operational disruption while maintaining safety
Supports passengers and protects operational continuity
Facilitates rapid recovery from irregular events

subsections.summary: Irregular Operations (IROPS) include flight delays, flight diversions, and flight cancellations.
key_points: IROPS include flight delays, diversions, and cancellations

sections.section_summary: Establishes procedures for managing irregular operations (IROPS) including delay classification, passenger communication, diversions, cancellations, and recovery operations. All IROPS events are coordinated through the Operations Control Center (OCC) with safety as the overriding priority.

subsections.summary: Categorizes delays into Weather, Technical, Crew, Airport, and Security types, each with specific causes.
key_points: Weather Delays: thunderstorms, fog, snow, strong winds
Technical Delays: aircraft defects, maintenance, equipment failures
Crew Delays: duty limitations, crew shortages, positioning issues
Airport Delays: congestion, gate availability, infrastructure issues
Security Delays: security incidents, screening requirements, law enforcement activity

subsections.summary: Defines the sequential steps to be taken upon identification of a significant delay.
key_points: OCC determines cause of delay
Impact assessment is completed
Passenger communications begin
Recovery options are evaluated
Operational updates continue until resolution

subsections.summary: Outlines requirements for communicating delay information to passengers, emphasizing accuracy and timeliness.
key_points: Passengers must receive accurate information and timely updates
Expected departure estimates must be provided
Recovery options must be communicated
Information must not be speculative or misleading

subsections.summary: Describes recovery measures to minimize passenger disruption following irregular operations.
key_points: Recovery measures include rebooking, alternate routing, accommodation, meal vouchers, and transportation support
Priority is given to minimizing passenger disruption

subsections.summary: Identifies causes of flight diversions and establishes that diversion decisions prioritize safety.
key_points: Diversion causes: weather, medical emergencies, security incidents, technical concerns, airport closures
Diversion decisions shall prioritize safety

subsections.summary: Defines the sequential response steps following a flight diversion.
key_points: Ground support shall be arranged
Passenger handling plans shall be activated
Fuel requirements shall be evaluated
Crew limitations shall be reviewed
Recovery planning shall begin

subsections.summary: Establishes that flight cancellations may only be approved by authorized personnel, with safety as the primary consideration.
key_points: Cancellations may only be approved by authorized personnel
Decisions consider safety, operational feasibility, resource availability, and passenger impact
Safety considerations shall always take precedence

subsections.summary: Outlines sequential steps to be taken upon flight cancellation.
key_points: Passenger notifications shall begin
Rebooking activities shall commence
Crew assignments shall be reviewed
Aircraft recovery plans shall be activated
Resource reallocation shall occur

subsections.summary: Describes aircraft recovery activities aimed at restoring network stability.
key_points: Recovery includes aircraft substitutions, schedule modifications, repositioning flights, and maintenance adjustments
Recovery efforts shall prioritize restoration of network stability

subsections.summary: Outlines crew recovery activities while maintaining compliance with duty regulations.
key_points: Activities include reassignments, reserve crew activation, positioning arrangements, and schedule adjustments
All actions shall remain compliant with duty regulations

subsections.summary: Defines network recovery planning considerations with the objective of restoring normal operations safely.
key_points: Considers fleet availability, crew availability, airport capacity, passenger demand, and operational priorities
Objective is restoration of normal operations as quickly as safely possible

subsections.summary: Describes customer service recovery measures with passenger welfare as a primary consideration.
key_points: Measures include travel credits, refunds, accommodation, meal assistance, and ground transportation
Passenger welfare shall remain a primary consideration

subsections.summary: Establishes documentation requirements for all irregular operations events.
key_points: All IROPS events shall be documented
Reports shall include cause, duration, operational impact, recovery actions, and passenger impact

subsections.summary: Outlines post-event review processes to support continuous improvement following significant disruptions.
key_points: Root causes shall be identified
Operational performance shall be reviewed
Corrective actions shall be developed
Lessons learned shall be documented
Continuous improvement opportunities shall be incorporated into future operations

subsections.summary: Defines key performance indicators for monitoring irregular operations performance.
key_points: Indicators include delay minutes, cancellation rates, diversion rates, passenger recovery times, and operational recovery effectiveness
Performance trends shall be reviewed regularly

sections.section_summary: Establishes a coordinated framework for responding to emergencies affecting passengers, crew, aircraft, facilities, personnel, or operations. Priorities include preservation of life, protection of property, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, and effective communication. References ICAO, FAA, and airport emergency planning standards.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of Emergency Response Procedures as establishing a coordinated framework for emergency response.
key_points: Prioritizes preservation of life, protection of property, operational continuity, regulatory compliance, and effective communication

subsections.summary: Identifies types of emergencies and establishes classification by severity and operational impact.
key_points: Emergencies include aircraft accidents, incidents, medical emergencies, fire, security incidents, natural disasters, hazardous material incidents, and airport evacuations
All emergencies shall be classified according to severity and operational impact

subsections.summary: Defines the notification sequence and required information upon identification of an emergency.
key_points: Notify OCC, emergency services, airport authorities, and senior management
Activate emergency response procedures
Notifications must include nature, location, time, personnel involved, and immediate hazards

subsections.summary: Describes activation and coordination functions of the Emergency Operations Center (EOC).
key_points: EOC may be activated during significant events
EOC coordinates operational response, resource allocation, stakeholder communication, regulatory coordination, and recovery activities
EOC shall remain active until emergency conditions are resolved

subsections.summary: Outlines response procedures in the event of an aircraft accident.
key_points: Activate emergency response plan and coordinate with emergency services
Establish communication channels and support rescue operations
Preserve evidence and support investigators
Only authorized personnel may release information regarding the accident

subsections.summary: Describes response to aircraft incidents that do not constitute full accidents.
key_points: Incidents include engine failures, emergency landings, system failures, ground collisions, and runway excursions
OCC shall coordinate response activities and provide operational support until resolved

subsections.summary: Establishes medical emergency procedures treating them as priority events.
key_points: Contact medical assistance and assess immediate risks
Coordinate emergency services and document actions taken
Medical confidentiality shall be maintained whenever possible

subsections.summary: Outlines response procedures for various fire emergencies.
key_points: Fire types: aircraft, terminal, ground equipment, and fuel-related fires
Raise alarm, notify emergency services, evacuate affected areas, and isolate hazards if safe
Personnel shall not place themselves at unnecessary risk

subsections.summary: Defines response procedures for bomb threats.
key_points: Record all available information and notify security personnel, OCC, and law enforcement
Follow evacuation instructions if required
Threats shall be treated seriously until assessed by competent authorities

subsections.summary: Outlines evacuation requirements and accountability procedures.
key_points: Evacuation may be required due to fire, security threats, structural hazards, hazardous materials, or natural disasters
Personnel shall guide passengers and staff to designated assembly areas
Accountability procedures shall be initiated immediately following evacuation

subsections.summary: Describes family assistance activities following major emergencies.
key_points: Activities include information centers, passenger status support, counseling support, and transportation assistance
Coordinated through designated response teams

subsections.summary: Establishes restrictions on media communications during emergencies.
key_points: Only authorized spokespersons may communicate with media organizations
Personnel shall not release passenger/crew information, investigation findings, or unverified information
Media communications shall be coordinated through approved channels

subsections.summary: Addresses maintenance of critical functions during emergencies.
key_points: Critical functions shall be maintained whenever possible
Planning addresses operational control, communication systems, personnel availability, and facility disruptions
Recovery activities shall begin as soon as conditions permit

subsections.summary: Outlines post-emergency review processes to support continuous improvement.
key_points: Investigations shall be conducted and lessons learned documented
Corrective actions shall be developed and emergency plans updated
Performance reviews shall support continuous improvement

subsections.summary: Establishes requirements for periodic testing of emergency response plans.
key_points: Plans tested through tabletop exercises, functional exercises, and full-scale drills
Results shall be documented and reviewed

sections.section_summary: Establishes procedures for the safe acceptance, handling, storage, transportation, loading, and reporting of hazardous materials transported by air. References ICAO Technical Instructions, IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, and FAA Hazardous Materials Guidance. All activities must comply with applicable regulatory requirements and safety standards.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of Dangerous Goods Management as ensuring safe handling of hazardous materials transported by air in compliance with regulatory requirements.
key_points: Covers acceptance, handling, storage, transportation, loading, and reporting of hazardous materials
Activities shall comply with all applicable regulatory requirements and safety standards

subsections.summary: Identifies the nine classes of dangerous goods as defined by international regulations.
key_points: Class 1: Explosives
Class 2: Gases
Class 3: Flammable Liquids
Class 4: Flammable Solids
Class 5: Oxidizing Substances
Class 6: Toxic and Infectious Substances
Class 7: Radioactive Materials
Class 8: Corrosive Materials
Class 9: Miscellaneous Dangerous Goods
Personnel shall be familiar with applicable classifications

subsections.summary: Establishes conditions under which dangerous goods may be accepted for air transport.
key_points: Goods must be properly declared, packaged, labeled, and documented
Goods must be authorized for air transport
Non-compliant shipments shall be rejected

subsections.summary: Identifies required documentation for dangerous goods shipments.
key_points: Documentation includes shipper declarations, transport documentation, emergency response information, and regulatory approvals
Documentation shall be verified before shipment acceptance

subsections.summary: Establishes packaging standards for dangerous goods shipments.
key_points: Packaging must meet regulatory standards and prevent leakage
Must protect contents and withstand transportation conditions
Damaged packaging shall not be accepted

subsections.summary: Defines labeling requirements for dangerous goods shipments.
key_points: Shipments shall display hazard labels, handling labels, identification markings, and regulatory markings
Incorrect labeling shall be corrected before transport

subsections.summary: Establishes requirements for dangerous goods storage areas.
key_points: Storage areas shall be secured, clearly identified, and maintain required segregation
Areas shall prevent unauthorized access
Incompatible materials shall not be stored together

sections.section_summary: This portion of Section 16 covers loading procedures, lithium battery handling, incident response, emergency response, reporting requirements, training requirements, and compliance monitoring for dangerous goods operations.

subsections.summary: Establishes requirements for safe loading of dangerous goods on aircraft.
key_points: Loading must comply with aircraft limitations, segregation requirements, quantity restrictions, and safety requirements
Loading personnel must follow approved loading instructions

subsections.summary: Defines verification and acceptance requirements for lithium batteries, which represent a significant transportation risk.
key_points: Personnel must verify packaging requirements, quantity limitations, documentation requirements, and regulatory compliance
Damaged batteries shall not be accepted

subsections.summary: Identifies types of dangerous goods incidents and notification requirements.
key_points: Incidents may include leaks, spills, packaging failures, and undeclared dangerous goods
Personnel must immediately notify supervisors and safety personnel

subsections.summary: Outlines the step-by-step response procedure for dangerous goods incidents.
key_points: Response steps: isolate the area, notify emergency responders, protect personnel, follow emergency guidance, and document the event
Personnel safety is the highest priority

subsections.summary: Defines reporting standards for dangerous goods incidents.
key_points: Reports must comply with regulatory requirements, company policy, and airport requirements
Reports must include complete details of the event

subsections.summary: Specifies training obligations for personnel involved with dangerous goods.
key_points: Personnel must receive initial training, recurrent training, and emergency response training
Training records must be maintained and monitored

subsections.summary: Defines methods for monitoring dangerous goods compliance.
key_points: Compliance monitoring includes audits, inspections, incident reviews, and performance assessments
Corrective actions must be implemented when deficiencies are identified

sections.section_summary: Establishes the framework for training governance, competency assessment, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, corrective actions, and continuous improvement to ensure personnel possess the knowledge, skills, and qualifications required for safe and compliant operations.

subsections.summary: Defines the purpose of the Training, Quality Assurance, and Compliance program.
key_points: Ensures personnel possess the knowledge, skills, qualifications, and competencies required to perform assigned duties safely and effectively
Maintains compliance with regulatory requirements and company standards

subsections.summary: Establishes that the Training Department shall maintain training programs for all operational personnel.
key_points: Programs must address initial qualification and recurrent qualification
Programs must address regulatory requirements, operational procedures, and safety requirements

subsections.summary: Requires new personnel to complete initial training before performing operational duties.
key_points: Training may include company orientation, operational procedures, safety requirements, security requirements, and emergency procedures
Successful completion must be documented

subsections.summary: Mandates recurrent training at established intervals to maintain competency.
key_points: Ensures knowledge retention, procedural compliance, regulatory compliance, and competency maintenance
Personnel failing recurrent training shall be removed from operational duties until compliance is restored

subsections.summary: Defines the methods used to assess personnel competency.
key_points: Assessments may include written examinations, practical evaluations, operational observations, and simulations
Assessment results must be documented and retained

subsections.summary: Specifies the information that must be included in training records.
key_points: Records must include course completion dates, qualifications, certifications, assessment results, and expiration dates
Records must be maintained securely and accurately

subsections.summary: Defines the scope of the Quality Assurance Program and its role in continuous improvement.
key_points: Program monitors operational compliance, procedural effectiveness, training effectiveness, and regulatory compliance
Quality assurance activities support continuous improvement

subsections.summary: Establishes the purpose and scope of internal audits.
key_points: Audits evaluate compliance with company procedures, regulatory requirements, safety requirements, and security requirements
Audit findings must be documented and tracked

subsections.summary: Outlines areas of regulatory compliance that must be monitored.
key_points: Compliance monitoring covers aviation regulations, airport requirements, security requirements, and safety requirements
Non-compliance issues must be addressed promptly

subsections.summary: Defines how corrective actions are developed and tracked.
key_points: Corrective actions must be developed for audit findings, incident investigations, compliance deficiencies, and operational concerns
Corrective actions must remain open until verified as effective

subsections.summary: Establishes requirements for management of operational documents.
key_points: Documents must be version controlled, reviewed periodically, approved before release, and distributed appropriately
Personnel must use only current approved documents

subsections.summary: Defines the process for collecting and applying lessons learned.
key_points: Lessons learned shall be collected from incidents, audits, operational reviews, and emergency events
Findings shall be incorporated into training and procedures

subsections.summary: Establishes metrics and review processes for monitoring training and compliance performance.
key_points: Monitoring includes training completion rates, audit results, compliance metrics, qualification status, and corrective action effectiveness
Performance trends shall be reviewed regularly

subsections.summary: Defines the organization's commitment to ongoing improvement.
key_points: Improvement activities include training enhancements, audit programs, safety reviews, operational feedback, and regulatory updates
Continuous improvement activities support safety, compliance, and operational excellence
